rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: Solana (spot)
positions.catalyst: Dated, verifiable, in-window network catalyst: Anza's Agave v4.2 mainnet FEATURE ACTIVATIONS unlock Monday August 17, 2026 — the largest protocol change since launch. Three feature-gated upgrades go live: a ~90% cut to on-chain rent, max transaction size raised from 1,232 to 4,096 bytes, and slot times halved from 400ms to 200ms (testnet is already running 300ms slots). The same release shipped the first public Alpenglow consensus codebase (Votor/Rotor, ~150ms finality) for an expected 4.3 activation. Layered on top: MoneyGram Ramps went live on Solana on Aug 10-11 — the remittance giant's cash network now supports crypto-to-cash payouts in 170+ countries and cash-in in 25+, after MoneyGram became a Solana validator in June. And the flow divergence is the cleanest signal in the complex: Solana spot ETFs took $8.8M net on Aug 10, the biggest single day since May 12 (BSOL absorbed nearly all of it, total SOL ETF net assets ~$906M) with another inflow Aug 11 via Morgan Stanley's MSOL — while spot BITCOIN ETFs just logged their first back-to-back outflow days since late July, roughly $192M out. Solana ETFs are +33% on 2026 cumulative inflows; Bitcoin ETFs are -5.5% with over $7B of outflows.
positions.driver: LONG spot SOL, 100% of capital, UNLEVERAGED — deliberately. US equity markets are closed (Saturday), so the mandate restricts the universe to spot crypto: no inverse ETFs, no 2x/3x crypto funds, long-only. That constraint matters because the crypto tape is outright weak — BTC is at ~$62,964 having ground down all Friday to a $62,470 intraday low, trading below EMA20 ($63,961), EMA50 ($64,463) and EMA200 ($71,907), with Fear & Greed at 29 and crypto pointedly NOT responding to the week's soft CPI/PPI/retail-sales data the way gold and silver did. On a long-only day into a downtrending tape, the right expression is the single name with a real forward catalyst and the least extension, sized without leverage. SOL is that name. The asymmetry: the downside is ordinary BTC-beta drift over a thin weekend, while the upside is a positioning bid into a hard-dated Monday morning mainnet activation that measurably improves the chain's economics (90% rent cut) and throughput (2x slot speed) — the kind of event that gets front-run in the 24-48 hours before it lands, which is exactly our holding window. Critically we are NOT chasing: SOL at 75.21 is DOWN on the session (it printed ~76.70 earlier), so we are buying the catalyst before the anticipation bid rather than after it — the opposite of the gap-chasing the mandate bans. Chosen over: (1) SPOT BTC — the lower-vol park, but it is the weakest chart in the complex (below every major MA, two straight days of ETF outflows, failing repeatedly at $65K with traders warning a weak weekly close invites more losses) and has zero forward catalyst; going all-in long the asset that is actively leading the group lower is negative asymmetry regardless of its lower volatility. (2) SPOT ETH at $1,878 — same beta problem as SOL but with no dated catalyst of its own; strictly dominated. (3) XRP at $1.0015 — sitting exactly on the psychological $1.00 handle with ETF assets at $1.51B and the CLARITY Act Senate vote not until September 15; the catalyst is a month away, not a day away, and $1.00 is a level that invites a stop-run. (4) BNB $611 / LINK $9.33 / LTC $44.03 / AVAX $6.57 / ADA $0.179 / DOGE $0.0699 — no fresh catalyst, thinner weekend books, and the small-cap alts carry gap risk that a 100%-of-capital book should not underwrite. (5) All leveraged crypto ETFs (BITX, 2X Solana) and every equity-listed instrument — hard-excluded, US markets closed Saturday. (6) 100% CASH — defensible given the tape, but SOL offers a genuine dated event rather than a coin-flip, so sitting out would forfeit the one real edge available today. Entry 75.21 = canonical dashboard live feed, asOf 2026-08-15T10:42:01Z, cross-checked against a 10:40:55Z pull at 75.20. Stop 67.69 (-10%, the spot band).
positions.risks: Beta is the main risk and it is not small: SOL is high-beta to BTC, so if bitcoin loses the $62.5K floor it has been testing all week, SOL falls harder than the index and the -10% stop can be reached on a move that is only about -5% in BTC. Weekend crypto books are thin, which cuts both ways — a low-liquidity flush can overshoot violently with no equity-market circuit breaker and, because the next rotation is Sunday morning, there is no ability to act on an intraday stop overnight. The catalyst is also NOT inside the holding window: Agave v4.2 activates Monday Aug 17 while we rotate Sunday morning, so this trade monetizes anticipation, not the event itself — a lower-quality edge, and if positioning simply does not build over a quiet weekend the trade is pure beta with no catalyst payoff. Event risk cuts the other way too: a botched or delayed feature activation, or any validator instability during the phased slot-time reduction, would hit SOL specifically and hard, since network reliability is Solana's historical bear case. Sentiment is genuinely poor (Fear & Greed 29) and the macro read that helped metals all week has actively failed to help crypto, so there is no reason to assume the soft-data tailwind arrives late. Mitigants: no leverage (the single biggest downside protection available today — a 10% adverse move costs 10%, not 20-30%), a -10% hard stop, an entry that is below the session's earlier print rather than chasing a gap, the largest and most liquid catalyst-bearing alt rather than a small cap, and a flow backdrop where SOL is taking ETF inflows while BTC is bleeding them.
